brief_text: I run operations at our bottling plant in Leeds, and the scrap rate on Line 2 is running at about 6.5% of bottles filled, which is costing us far too much. I want to bring it down to 4% or lower by the end of June next year. The options on the table are: retrofit the filler with new vision inspection cameras (the supplier quotes £180k and reckons it would cut scrap by 1.5 to 2.5 percentage points), run a structured operator retraining programme on the night shift, where most of the rejects happen, or switch to a lighter preform supplier whose bottles are cheaper but whose defect rates we haven't tested properly. We have £200k of capital left this financial year, so we can't do the cameras and anything else big. The main risk is that the camera retrofit takes Line 2 down for around three weeks, and we're already tight on summer stock. Honestly, I'd rather not change the preform supplier unless we have to, because the last switch was painful.
